@d-t-w thanks.. I still think about how to best "fix" this. For me we have 3 issues:
- We should not have ChannelPipeline block like this.
- Maybe doing the pining how we do is not a good idea here
- The next() call should not use round-robin for the DefaultEvenExecutorGroup

@normanmaurer can I ask, why is it important to have the addLast to the pipeline be executed by the EventExecutor that is supplied in the method call? Is it acceptable to have all channel initialization performed by the parent (NIO in this case) event group and limit the scope of the custom EventExecutorGroup to just execution of the handler?

It is important because otherwise the life-cycle methods of the ChannelHandler (like ChannelHandler.beforeAdd(..)) are not executed by the correct thread. The same is true for the remove/replace operations. 

So there are two possibilities here to fix it :
- Let each of the add/remove/replace operation return a ChannelFuture which is notified once the operation completes
- Just schedule the execution of the lifecycle operations and log it if an error occur. 

I think I would do the first.

I did some more thinking and I think return a ChannelFuture also sucks in terms that a user need to build up some kind of very complex listener chain if he want to add many ChannelHandler and be sure they are added in the correct order. 

So at the moment I'm about to suggest that we add the handlers in the pipeline and only execute the life-cycle-methods via the EventLoopExecutor or direct if we are in the correct EventLoop. If any exception occur we just call  fireExceptionCaught.
